reference.one_line: 54-year-old woman, day 2 of heparin for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism with right leg clot; stable and improving, but this morning's anti-Xa of 0.86 is unactioned.

handoff.summary: Sigrun Skjelbred, 54, has clots in both lungs with right heart strain and a right popliteal and femoral vein thrombosis after knee arthroscopy, a 14-hour flight and oral hormone therapy. Blood pressure has never been below 108 systolic; heart rate is down from 118 to 88 and oxygen from 4 L to 1 L, though she falls to 87% walking 25 m on 2 L. The 08:05 anti-Xa is 0.86 (target 0.30 to 0.70) but heparin is still at 1,650 units/h and the progress note records 0.68; gum bleeding, a 3 cm bruise and a pink-stained tissue are charted today. Her oestrogen tablet is still being given against the response team's advice.
to_do: Reduce heparin to 1,500 units/h now (two-nurse check); repeat anti-Xa 6 hours later
Discontinue estradiol/norethindrone before the 18 Nov 09:00 dose
Tell the response team at the 15:00 re-review and correct the progress note
If no procedure is needed, apixaban 10 mg twice daily from 18 Nov, stopping heparin with the first tablet
if_then: If systolic falls below 100, heart rate exceeds 120, oxygen exceeds 6 L or she faints, then call the team and the response team at once
If the repeat anti-Xa is above 0.90, then stop the infusion for 1 hour and restart 3 units/kg/h lower
If a nosebleed does not stop, or there is black stool, blood in urine or new headache, then stop heparin, send a blood count and call the resident

reference.brief_hospital_course: Mrs Skjelbred, 54, presented on 16 Nov at 05:40 with breathlessness, pleuritic right chest pain and a near-faint on the stairs, saturating 88% on room air. On closer questioning her right calf had ached since 11 Nov, the day after a 14-hour flight, and she had been breathless on stairs since 12 Nov; she had telephoned the orthopaedic clinic on 13 Nov. Other risk factors were right knee arthroscopy on 27 Oct and combined oral hormone therapy. CT showed emboli in both lungs with a ventricle ratio of 1.4, echo confirmed right ventricular strain, troponin peaked at 74 ng/L and ultrasound showed occlusive right popliteal and femoral vein thrombosis. Blood pressure stayed at or above 108 systolic, and the embolism response team advised anticoagulation alone with catheter treatment in reserve. Weight-based heparin was started and increased to 1,650 units/h after a first anti-Xa of 0.24. On 17 Nov the level was 0.86 with minor gum and nasal bleeding, requiring a rate reduction. Oxygen need fell from 4 L to 1 L and markers improved. Hormone therapy, continued in error on admission, is to stop permanently; amlodipine and ibuprofen were held. Apixaban is planned from 18 Nov and discharge on 19 or 20 Nov.

problem_list.problem: Acute pulmonary embolism, both lungs, with right heart strain (intermediate-high risk)
Deep vein thrombosis, right popliteal and femoral veins

evidence: vitals: 88% on room air 16 Nov 06:00; 96% on 1 L 17 Nov 12:00

problem_list.problem: Heparin above target (anti-Xa 0.86, rate not reduced) with new minor bleeding
Menopausal flushes on oestrogen-containing therapy, now contraindicated but still charted

reconciled_medications.reason: Anti-Xa 0.86: protocol says decrease 150 units/h to 1,500 and recheck in 6 hours; stop when apixaban starts.
Oestrogen promotes clotting; response team said stop and do not restart.
Long-term treatment, no conflict with the plan.
Protect blood pressure while the right heart is strained; review in primary care.

pending_items: Heparin rate reduction and repeat anti-Xa (overdue since about 09:50)
Response team re-review 17 Nov 15:00: is any procedure needed?
Community pharmacy check of home medicine list (no result recorded)
Walking saturation 18 Nov; home oxygen assessment if below 88% on room air
Clot clinic within 2 weeks, primary care within 1 week; her question about knee physiotherapy

qa.q: What heparin bolus and starting rate did she receive, and when?
qa.a: 6,500 units at 07:30 on 16 Nov, then 1,500 units/h (15 mL/h) from 07:35.

qa.q: What was the ventricle ratio on CT and the estimated pulmonary artery pressure on echo?
qa.a: Right-to-left ratio 1.4; pulmonary artery systolic pressure about 52 mmHg.

qa.q: How have the anti-Xa levels run?

qa.a: Yes: troponin 68, peak 74, then 41 ng/L; BNP 612 then 388 pg/mL; lactate 1.9 then 1.1.

qa.q: How has her oxygen requirement changed?
qa.a: 4 L in the emergency department, 3 L from 10:00 on 16 Nov, 2 L from 20:00, 1 L (96%) at 12:00 on 17 Nov; still 87% walking 25 m on 2 L.

qa.q: How long since the high level was drawn, and since the last rate change?
qa.a: Drawn 08:05, about 6.5 hours ago; the rate has been 1,650 units/h since 14:20 on 16 Nov, about 24 hours.

qa.q: When did symptoms begin relative to the flight and admission?
qa.a: Landed 10 Nov; calf ache 11 Nov; breathless on stairs 12 Nov; phoned the clinic 13 Nov; admitted 16 Nov. About five days, not one hour.

qa.q: What does the protocol require for an anti-Xa of 0.86?
qa.a: Decrease 2 units/kg/h (150 units/h for her) to 1,500 units/h within an hour and repeat the level in 6 hours.

qa.q: Why no clot-dissolving drug despite right heart strain?
qa.a: Blood pressure is stable, so bleeding risk outweighs benefit; knee surgery 20 days earlier is a relative contraindication. Catheter treatment is the rescue if she deteriorates.
evidence: notes: response team consult items 1 and 2

qa.q: Did the community pharmacy confirm her home medicine list?
qa.a: The chart does not say. A technician was to call on the afternoon of 16 Nov; no result is recorded.

qa.q: Who was told about the 0.86 result, and when?
qa.a: Not documented. It resulted at 08:50; no call or acknowledgement is recorded and the progress note quotes 0.68.

qa.q: Has she been tested for an inherited clotting tendency?
qa.a: No results exist; the response team advised against testing during the acute event.

tasks.prompt: Check the heparin infusion against the monitoring protocol and today's results.
expected_findings: Anti-Xa at 08:05 on 17 Nov is 0.86, above the 0.30 to 0.70 target
Protocol: decrease 150 units/h to 1,500 within 1 hour, repeat level in 6 hours
Rate still 1,650 units/h at 14:30 (last change 16 Nov 14:20), with new minor bleeding charted
acceptable_actions: Reduce to 1,500 units/h with a two-nurse check and order a repeat anti-Xa
Notify the resident and response team; continue bleeding checks and blood count
must_not: Leave the rate because the progress note says the level is in range
Stop anticoagulation altogether, or bolus or increase heparin

tasks.prompt: Review the active medication orders against the diagnosis and the consultants' advice.
expected_findings: Estradiol/norethindrone ordered 16 Nov 11:10, given 16 and 17 Nov, due again 18 Nov 09:00
Oestrogen promotes clotting; the response team said at 12:30 on 16 Nov to stop it and not restart
acceptable_actions: Discontinue the order and remove it from the discharge list
Tell the patient; arrange a non-oestrogen option for flushes
must_not: Continue it as a routine home medicine
Flag levothyroxine or atorvastatin, or restart amlodipine or ibuprofen

tasks.prompt: Verify the figures quoted in today's progress note against the source results.
expected_findings: The 09:40 note says 'Anti-Xa this morning 0.68, in range' and 'no change needed'
The laboratory value drawn 08:05 is 0.86; the digits are transposed
The wrong figure explains why the rate was not adjusted
acceptable_actions: Correct or addend the note and inform the resident
Act on the true value per protocol
must_not: Call the overnight values 0.52 and 0.48 errors

tasks.prompt: Reconstruct the timeline of this illness from all sources and compare it with the admission history.
expected_findings: Admission history: well until 04:30 on 16 Nov, no leg pain
Other sources: calf ache from 11 Nov, breathless on stairs from 12 Nov, clinic call 13 Nov with no ultrasound arranged; ultrasound shows clot days old
A subacute five-day presentation with a missed warning call
acceptable_actions: Correct the history in the record
Feed back the missed call to the orthopaedic clinic
must_not: State that symptoms began on the morning of admission
Conclude the longer history removes the need for anticoagulation
evidence: notes: response team consult; night nursing note

tasks.prompt: Assess whether the treatment intensity chosen for this pulmonary embolism is appropriate.
expected_findings: Right heart strain and raised troponin with stable pressure (never below 108 systolic) is intermediate-high risk
Anticoagulation with monitoring is standard; thrombolysis is kept for deterioration, and recent knee surgery adds bleeding risk
The reasoning and escalation triggers are documented
acceptable_actions: Confirm the plan is appropriate and keep the escalation triggers
must_not: Flag the absence of thrombolysis as an error
Recommend systemic clot-dissolving treatment while she is stable

epilogue.note: What happens AFTER 'now' in this simulated world. Never shown in the chart; for outcome-prediction ground truth.
epilogue.course: At the 15:00 re-review Dr. Brandvold read the laboratory value herself, saw 0.86 with new bruising and asked why the rate was unchanged. The infusion was reduced to 1,500 units/h at 15:20, the hormone therapy order was discontinued and the resident addended his note. A nosebleed at 15:50 stopped after ten minutes of pressure. The repeat anti-Xa was 0.58 and haemoglobin held at 12.3. No procedure was needed; apixaban 10 mg twice daily replaced heparin on 18 Nov. Oxygen came off slowly: 88% walking on 1 L on 18 Nov, 91% on room air on 20 Nov, when she went home without oxygen. Three days later a withdrawal bleed after stopping the hormones, heavier on apixaban, was managed in clinic (haemoglobin 11.8) without interrupting treatment.

events.event: Response team finds anti-Xa 0.86 unactioned; heparin reduced to 1,500 units/h; hormone therapy discontinued
Nosebleed, stopped after 10 minutes of pressure
First apixaban 10 mg given; heparin stopped. Haemoglobin 12.3 g/dL
Walking saturation 91% on room air after 60 m
Discharged home on apixaban, no home oxygen
Clot clinic same-day visit for withdrawal bleed: haemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, apixaban continued
Apixaban reduced to 5 mg twice daily as planned

outcomes_30_day.notable: Withdrawal bleed on apixaban after stopping hormone therapy, managed in clinic; January work trip postponed.

portal_messages.subject: Calf tight since flying home - normal after the knee op?
portal_messages.body: Hello, I had my knee keyhole surgery on 27 October and flew back from Seoul on Tuesday. Since yesterday my right calf (same leg) has been aching and tight, like cramp that will not go. Today I was puffed going up the stairs, which is not like me. Is this just swelling from the flight? Should I wait for my next appointment? Thank you, Sigrun
ideal_reply_points: Calf pain plus new breathlessness after surgery and a long flight needs same-day assessment for a clot
Urgent ultrasound or emergency department today; ambulance for chest pain or fainting
Do not reassure with elevation and ice alone

portal_messages.subject: Question about Sigrun's hormone tablets
portal_messages.body: This is Anselm, Sigrun's husband, writing from her account with her beside me. The lung clot doctor told us yesterday her hormone tablets for hot flushes make clots more likely and she should come off them. But she was given one this morning with her other pills. Is she meant to keep taking them? We did not want to make a fuss. Also her gums bled a bit today.
ideal_reply_points: They are right: the tablet should have been stopped; stop the order today
Gum bleeding on heparin should be told to the nurse now; the heparin level will be checked
Flushes can be treated without oestrogen

portal_messages.subject: Re: Question about Sigrun's hormone tablets
portal_messages.body: Dear Mr and Mrs Skjelbred, you were right to ask. The hormone tablet has now been stopped and should not be restarted at home; I am sorry it was given. We also found this morning's heparin level was higher than we want, which fits with the gum bleeding, and the drip has been turned down. Please ring the bell for a nosebleed that lasts, black stools or a new headache. Dr. Olorunfemi
ideal_reply_points: Acknowledges the error plainly and says what changed

portal_messages.subject: Bleeding since stopping hormones
portal_messages.body: I came home on Friday on the apixaban, two tablets morning and night. Since Saturday evening I have been bleeding like a heavy period, which I have not had for two years. I change a pad about every three hours and there were clots this morning. No dizziness, breathing the same. Is this the blood thinner? I am nervous about carrying on with it but more nervous about stopping.
ideal_reply_points: Do not stop apixaban on her own
Likely a withdrawal bleed after stopping hormones, heavier on an anticoagulant
Same-day blood count and review; emergency department if soaking a pad an hour, faint or more breathless

conversation.setting: Bedside on 3 West (3W-07), 16 Nov about 12:15, embolism response team review; husband present

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Mrs Skjelbred? I'm Dr. Brandvold, one of the lung doctors, from the team that looks at bigger clots. Is now all right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. Sorry, I run out of puff if I talk too long.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Short answers are fine. I've read the notes, but I'd like to hear it from you. When did you last feel completely well?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, it happened this morning. Half past four. I woke up and couldn't get my breath, and on the stairs I nearly went.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: That's when it got frightening. Before that, though. Anything in the leg?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The knee's fine. The calf's been... well, aching.

turns.speaker: husband
turns.text: Since the flight. You said on the Wednesday it felt like cramp.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The day after I landed, yes. The eleventh. I thought it was from sitting fourteen hours.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: And your breathing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Puffed on the stairs from, um, Thursday. I rang the knee clinic on Friday about it.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: You rang them. What did they say?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That swelling's common after the operation and flying. Put it up, ice it, ring back if it's worse.

turns.speaker: husband
turns.text: Nobody mentioned a scan.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: That matters, thank you. Let me say it back: calf from the eleventh, breathless from the twelfth, you called on the thirteenth, and this morning you nearly fainted. Five days, not one morning. Right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. I told the doctor downstairs it started today because that's when it was bad.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: A natural way to tell it. Now, your tablets. There's one for hot flushes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The hormone one, two years now. It's been a lifesaver, honestly.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: I believe you. The trouble is the oestrogen in it makes blood more likely to clot. I'd like it stopped from now, and not restarted.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh. They gave me one about ten minutes ago with the others.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Then that should be the last. I'll write it clearly for the ward team.

turns.speaker: husband
turns.text: Can I ask... they said her heart's under strain. Shouldn't she be getting the clot-buster drug?

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Fair question; the heart doctors, the X-ray doctors and I have just discussed exactly that. Her blood pressure has held, never under 108 on the top number. In that situation the clot-buster does more harm from bleeding than good, more so three weeks after knee surgery.

turns.speaker: husband
turns.text: So just the drip.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: The heparin drip, with close watching. If her pressure dropped, or she fainted, or needed a lot more oxygen, we can treat the clot through a thin tube, and we'd move fast.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: How long on the drip?

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: A day or two, to keep our options open, then a tablet for at least three months. Tell me what you'll watch for, so I know I've explained it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Bleeding. Nose, wee, black stools. And a headache.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Exactly. And if you feel faint, bell straight away.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My mother had a leg clot after her hip. Should I be tested?

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: Not now; those tests are unreliable in the middle of a clot. I'll be back tomorrow at three.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you for asking about the leg. I thought I was making a fuss.

turns.speaker: Dr. Brandvold
turns.text: You weren't. Ringing was the right thing.
